A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DecompDPO study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original CrossDocked2020 molecule-generation and optimization results, ablations, and molecular-property analyses in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original generation and optimization experiments, including single-objective alignment and additional conformation analyses in Section 4 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: v2 introduces physically constrained preference construction: bond-length and bond-angle penalties are subtracted from property rewards, changing the preferences used for optimization (Section 3.3). The DecompDiff* backbone, local/global DPO framework, bond-first noise schedule, and linear beta schedule already exist in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use CrossDocked2020 for protein-conditioned molecule generation and target-specific molecular optimization. The single-objective experiment and replacement molecular examples remain within this coverage; no new dataset, domain, or input scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: v2 adds IPDiff to generation and conformation comparisons and introduces a direct comparison with the preference-alignment method AliDiff in Table 3. RGA and DecompOpt remain in the main optimization comparison but disappear from the property boxplots (v1 Figure 7 versus v2 Figure 9).

E3.justification: Reported fine-tuning beta changes from 0.01 to 0.001, and optimization candidate pools decrease from 1,000 to 500 molecules. Checkpoint selection changes from three reported criteria to Success Rate multiplied by Complete Rate. Decomposition/beta ablations shift from optimization on 40 pockets to molecule generation. v2 also introduces Vina-only optimization and bond-angle/whole-molecule evaluation protocols. These reported changes do not establish that every retained result was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds single-objective alignment, bond-angle JSD, and whole-molecule MMFF RMSD/energy analyses, and replaces the optimization-setting decomposition/beta ablations with generation-setting ablations. The validity-guidance comparison and reference-model ablation disappear, although the guided result survives in the main optimization table. Decomposability correlations and multi-objective trade-off analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use boxplots, described in the text as confidence intervals, without documenting repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence levels, or significance tests. Changed plotted methods, populations, and values do not introduce a different statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Generation Success Rate changes from 36.9% to 36.2%, and median High Affinity from 93.8% to 95.2%, alongside revised settings. v2's optimization row, including 52.1% Success Rate and -7.27 mean Vina Score, exactly matches v1's validity-guidance row rather than establishing a new gain. Single-objective, angle, and whole-molecule results are added; ablation, bond-distance, and generation completion/uniqueness entries also change.

T1.justification: v2 adds mathematical definitions of bond/angle penalties beyond three empirical standard deviations and the adjusted reward (Section 3.3). It removes v1's assertion that LocalDPO upper-bounds Diffusion-DPO in an extreme preference-conflict case. The principal DPO derivations remain, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about multi-granularity preference alignment and its two applications remain. v2 adds physics-informed conformation preservation as an explicit contribution and reports revised headline results separately for generation and optimization in the abstract and introduction.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking physical penalties to conformation preservation and decomposed preferences to mitigating objective conflicts. It removes v1's collision/disabled-guidance explanation and the claim that optimization is unrestricted by reference-model capability and optimal for the supplied pairs. Optimization Success Rate is now described as comparable to DecompOpt. The limitations paragraph is retained unchanged in Appendix B.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the constraint weight as 0.1, discloses approximately 16,000 fine-tuning steps, and reports A40 hardware for fine-tuning instead of V100. It removes statements excluding bond log-probabilities from affinity alignment and disabling validity guidance. Reproducibility remains ambiguous because Section 4.1 describes reciprocal-distance objective weights while Appendix C.4 retains exponential weights.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantive positioning against concurrent AliDiff work, distinguishing multi-objective alignment, conformation constraints, and iterative optimization while retaining the first-alignment claim. It adds Wu et al. as motivation for physical constraints and removes the GPT-4, Llama, AutoDock Vina 1.2, and Harris et al. pose-benchmarking references.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory motivation, method exposition, and results narrative are extensively rewritten. Decomposability motivation precedes GlobalDPO, physical constraints receive a new subsection, generation and optimization results are separated, and limitations move into the appendix. Citation style and heading conventions also change throughout.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the method schematic and decomposition illustration, splits the main results table, replaces molecular examples, and adds an angle table and whole-molecule plots. Correlation findings are redisplayed rather than newly introduced. The document template changes throughout; Figure 10 also swaps QED/SA panel order without correcting its left/right caption.

improvement.justification: The AliDiff comparison addresses a missing comparison with another SBDD preference-alignment method, while additional conformation tests make molecular-quality assessment more complete. Clearer method exposition also helps. These gains are limited by lost guidance/reference-model ablation comparisons and inconsistent objective-weight descriptions. No isolated ablation establishes the new penalty's benefit, and v2's main optimization row already appears in v1's guided results.
